tickets.title: Three holes in the citation guard, which is the hallucination guard the whole product's trustworthiness rests on. (1) NO MINIMUM QUOTE LENGTH and no word-boundary requirement: a single-character quote 'a' is cited against every document, so a degenerate quote is a universal citation. (2) The _source_doc cross-document fallback means a quote drawn from a DIFFERENT document is KEPT and silently RE-ATTRIBUTED to the fact's document — url, source_kind and published_at all taken from the wrong doc. The guard therefore certifies 'this span exists somewhere in this batch', not 'in the document this fact is about'. (3) A typographic apostrophe is a FALSE NEGATIVE: normalize_ws collapses whitespace and casefolds but does not normalise Unicode punctuation, so a curly apostrophe drops a legitimate fact. The guard correctly drops paraphrases, ellipsis-joins, one-word changes and empty quotes.

The guard therefore certifies 'this span exists somewhere in this batch', not 'in the document this fact is about'. (3) A typographic apostrophe is a FALSE NEGATIVE: normalize_ws collapses whitespace and casefolds but does not normalise Unicode punctuation, so a curly apostrophe drops a legitimate fact. The guard correctly drops paraphrases, ellipsis-joins, one-word changes and empty quotes.
tickets.reproduction: Verifier's exercise_extract.py, 13 probes against real documents. Single character 'a' -> KEPT, is_cited true against both documents. Quote from doc D1 with doc_id='D1' on a fact about D2 -> KEPT and re-attributed to D2. 'Jane O’Neil' vs source "O'Neil" -> dropped.

scheduling_constraints: HOURS.md is ORCHESTRATOR-OWNED (intake divergence). EXECUTION.md 8 declares it append-only and ownership-exempt; that makes it a shared write surface every ticket touches, which is exactly the collision the per-file predicate exists to prevent. The orchestrator appends one line per ticket at merge time. No worker writes it.
src/arrival/__main__.py is owned by T-0 (stub) and then T-6 (fills `build`). T-0 closes before any dispatch, so the two are never in flight together.
README.md is owned by T-0 (skeleton) and then T-9 (final). Same reasoning.
tests/fixtures/http/ is split by filename prefix: T-0 owns fixture_dossier_docs_*.json, T-1 owns {kind}_*.json. Disjoint, and T-0 closes first.

src/arrival/contracts.py, util.py, config.py are T-0's and are FROZEN-BY-CONVENTION for the run: no other ticket may edit them. A ticket that needs a contract change escalates; it does not fork the model.
SHARED SURFACE beyond globs: the SourceKind literal (contracts, T-0) is consumed by T-1 connectors and T-4 DISPLAYABLE_KINDS. T-0 pins the full literal up front so neither can widen it.
